next_step: Run one matched end-to-end evaluation on an independently sampled workload from the intended task family. Compare the retained scaffold with the best conventional baseline, counting acquisition and preparation costs as well as execution cost; use the same tasks and hardware, and report uncertainty in total cost.
allocation: One worker defines the workload sample, comparator, and profiling protocol; one measures acquisition/preparation and runs the paired evaluation.
decisive_observation: Whether the scaffold’s total cost, including acquisition and preparation, is lower than the conventional baseline across the sampled future tasks, with uncertainty small enough to support that comparison.

outcome_decisions.lower: Continue evaluating the scaffold for this family and test whether the advantage persists on another independent sample.
outcome_decisions.not_lower_or_uncertain: Do not claim a cost reduction; retain the correct scaffold and investigate alternative representations or better-matched workloads before investing in generalization.

retained_result: Preserve the seven-point agreement and the conditional thin-representation result. The operation-count disadvantage applies to the tested degree-four n=4 interpreter workload; it does not establish performance on other workloads.
uncertainty: The intended future workload distribution and acquisition cost are unmeasured. Interpreter counts do not establish wall-time gains, and the conventional method may use the same thin representation.
